title: SaiData Schema v0.3
description: Comprehensive schema for defining software metadata, installation methods, and provider-specific configurations. Supports multiple installation approaches: package managers, source builds, binary downloads, and installation scripts. Includes hierarchical configuration with OS-specific overrides and provider customizations.

metadata.description: Core metadata about the software being described. This section provides essential information for identification, categorization, and discovery

name.description: Unique identifier for the software. Used as the primary key for lookups and file naming. Should be lowercase, alphanumeric with hyphens

display_name.description: Human-readable name for display in UIs and documentation. Can include proper capitalization and spacing

description.description: Brief description of the software's purpose and functionality. Should be concise (1-2 sentences)
examples: High-performance HTTP server and reverse proxy
Tool for defining and running multi-container Docker applications

version.description: Default or recommended version of the software. Can be overridden in specific installation method definitions

category.description: Primary category for software classification. Used for organization and filtering

subcategory.description: More specific classification within the primary category

tags.description: Searchable keywords for discovery and filtering. Include technology stack, use cases, and features

license.description: Software license identifier. Use SPDX identifiers when possible

language.description: Primary programming language the software is written in

maintainer.description: Organization or individual maintaining the software

urls.description: Collection of relevant URLs for the software (website, documentation, source code, etc.)

security.description: Security-related metadata including vulnerability disclosure, signing keys, and SBOM information

saidata.description: Metadata about the saidata file generation and lifecycle

model.description: Name of the LLM model used to generate this saidata

generation_date.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when this saidata was generated

generation_time.description: Time taken to generate this saidata in seconds

test_date.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when this saidata was last tested

human_review_date.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when this saidata was last reviewed by a human

packages.description: Default package definitions that apply across providers

services.description: Default service definitions that apply across providers

files.description: Default file definitions that apply across providers

directories.description: Default directory definitions that apply across providers

commands.description: Default command definitions that apply across providers

ports.description: Default port definitions that apply across providers

containers.description: Default container definitions that apply across providers

sources.description: Default source build definitions that apply across providers. Used for building software from source code with various build systems (autotools, cmake, make, etc.)

binaries.description: Default binary download definitions that apply across providers. Used for downloading pre-compiled binaries with OS/architecture templating support

scripts.description: Default script installation definitions that apply across providers. Used for executing installation scripts with security measures and environment variable support

providers.description: Provider-specific configurations that override or extend default resource definitions. Each key is a provider name (e.g., 'apt', 'brew', 'dnf', 'docker', 'source', 'binary', 'script'). Provider configurations take precedence over defaults in the template resolution hierarchy

compatibility.description: Compatibility information defining which providers, platforms, architectures, and OS versions are supported. Used for validation and provider selection

matrix.description: Compatibility matrix showing which providers work on which platforms, architectures, and OS versions. Each entry defines support status, testing status, and recommendations

versions.description: Version information including latest, minimum supported, and LTS versions

provider_config.description: Provider-specific configuration that overrides or extends default resource definitions. All resource types defined here take precedence over defaults in the template resolution hierarchy

prerequisites.description: Required packages that must be installed before this provider can be used. Commonly used for build tools, compilers, and development libraries

build_commands.description: Custom build commands specific to this provider. Used primarily with source provider for non-standard build processes

packages.description: Provider-specific package definitions that override defaults. Use this to specify different package names, versions, or options for specific providers

package_sources.description: Defines multiple package sources with priorities and recommendations. Useful when software is available from multiple repositories (official, backports, third-party)

repositories.description: Repository definitions for adding third-party or official software repositories. Includes repository URLs, GPG keys, and resource overrides specific to that repository

services.description: Provider-specific service definitions. Override service names, types, or configurations for specific providers

files.description: Provider-specific file definitions. Override file paths, permissions, or types for specific providers

directories.description: Provider-specific directory definitions. Override directory paths, permissions, or ownership for specific providers

commands.description: Provider-specific command definitions. Override command paths or arguments for specific providers

ports.description: Provider-specific port definitions. Override port numbers or protocols for specific providers

containers.description: Provider-specific container definitions. Override container images, tags, or configurations for specific providers

sources.description: Provider-specific source build configurations that override or extend default sources

binaries.description: Provider-specific binary download configurations that override or extend default binaries

scripts.description: Provider-specific script installation configurations that override or extend default scripts

package.description: Package definition for package manager-based installations. Distinguishes between logical names (f cross-referencing) and actual package names (for installation)

name.tion: Logical name used as key for OS overrides and provider-specific configurations. Used in template functions like {{sai_package(0, 'name')}}

package_name.description: Actual package name used by package managers (apt, dnf, brew, etc.). This is what gets passed to 'apt install', 'dnf install', etc. Used in template functions like {{sai_package(0, 'package_name', 'apt')}}

version.description: Specific version to install. If omitted, the latest available version is used

alternatives.description: Alternative package names that provide similar functionality. Used as fallbacks if the primary package is unavailable

install_options.description: Additional options passed to the package manager during installation

repository.description: Specific repository name to use for this package. References a repository defined in the repositories array

checksum.description: Expected checksum for package verification. Format: algorithm:hash

signature.description: GPG signature URL or fingerprint for package verification

download_url.description: Direct download URL for the package file. Used when package is not available through standard repositories

service.description: Service definition for managing system services. Supports multiple service management systems across different platforms

name.description: Logical name for the service. Used in template functions like {{sai_service(0, 'name')}}

service_name.description: Actual service name used by the service manager (systemd, init, launchd, etc.). This is what gets passed to 'systemctl', 'service', etc. Used in template functions like {{sai_service(0, 'service_name')}}

type.description: Service management system type. Determines which commands are used for service operations (start, stop, restart, etc.)

enabled.description: Whether the service should be enabled to start automatically on boot. Defaults to false

config_files.description: List of configuration file paths associated with this service. Used for configuration management and validation

name.description: Logical name for the file (e.g., config, dotconf, log, data, binary)
Logical name for the directory (e.g., config, dotconf, log, data, lib)

command.description: Command-line executable definition. Tracks installed commands, their locations, and associated metadata

name.description: Logical name for the command. Used in template functions like {{sai_command(0, 'name')}}

path.description: Full path to the command executable. Used in template functions like {{sai_command(0, 'path')}}

arguments.description: Default arguments or common usage patterns for the command

aliases.description: Alternative names or symlinks for the command

shell_completion.description: Whether shell completion is available for this command

man_page.description: Manual page name or path for documentation

port.description: Network port definition. Tracks ports used by the software for network communication
Port number (1-65535). Used in template functions like {{sai_port(0, 'port')}}

protocol.description: Network protocol used by this port

service.description: Service or purpose of this port

description.description: Human-readable description of what this port is used for

container.description: Container definition for Docker/Podman-based deployments. Defines container images, configurations, and runtime parameters

name.description: Container name. Used in template functions like {{container_name}}

image.description: Container image name without tag or registry. Combined with registry and tag to form the full image reference

tag.description: Image tag/version. Defaults to 'latest' if not specified

registry.description: Container registry URL. Defaults to Docker Hub if not specified

platform.description: Target platform for multi-architecture images. Format: os/architecture

ports.description: Port mappings in Docker format. Format: [host_ip:]host_port:container_port[/protocol]

volumes.description: Volume mounts in Docker format. Format: [host_path:]container_path[:options]

environment.description: Environment variables passed to the container. Key-value pairs

networks.description: Docker networks to connect the container to

labels.description: Container labels for metadata and organization. Key-value pairs

source.description: Source build configuration for compiling software from source code

name.description: Logical name for the source build (e.g., main, stable, dev). Used for referencing in template functions and provider configurations

url.description: Source code download URL. Supports templating with {{version}}, {{platform}}, {{architecture}} placeholders

version.description: Version to build. Used in URL templating and for version detection

build_system.description: Build system type. Determines the default build commands used by the source provider

build_dir.description: Directory for building. Defaults to /tmp/sai-build-{software-name} if not specified

source_dir.description: Directory containing extracted source code. Auto-detected from archive structure if not specified

install_prefix.description: Installation prefix for compiled binaries and files. Defaults to /usr/local

configure_args.description: Arguments passed to the configure step (autotools/cmake)

build_args.description: Arguments passed to the build step (make/ninja)

install_args.description: Arguments passed to the install step

prerequisites.description: Required packages/tools that must be installed before building

environment.description: Environment variables set during the build process

checksum.description: Expected checksum of source archive for integrity verification. Format: algorithm:hash

custom_commands.description: Custom commands that override default build system behavior

download.description: Custom command to download source code. Overrides default wget/curl behavior

extract.description: Custom command to extract downloaded archive. Overrides default tar/unzip behavior

configure.description: Custom configure command. Overrides default autotools/cmake configure step

build.description: Custom build command. Overrides default make/ninja build step

install.description: Custom install command. Overrides default make install behavior

uninstall.description: Custom uninstall command for removing installed files

version.description: Command to get installed version for tracking

binary.description: Binary download configuration for installing pre-compiled executables

name.description: Logical name for the binary download (e.g., main, stable, dev). Used for referencing in template functions

url.description: Binary download URL. Supports templating with {{version}}, {{platform}}, {{architecture}} placeholders. Platform values: linux, darwin, windows. Architecture values: amd64, arm64, 386

version.description: Version to download. Used in URL templating and for version tracking

architecture.description: Target architecture. Auto-detected if not specified. Common values: amd64, arm64, 386

platform.description: Target platform/OS. Auto-detected if not specified. Common values: linux, darwin, windows

checksum.description: Expected checksum of binary file for integrity verification. Format: algorithm:hash

install_path.description: Installation directory for the binary. Defaults to /usr/local/bin

executable.description: Executable name within archive or final executable name. Defaults to software name

archive.description: Archive extraction configuration for compressed binary downloads

format.description: Archive format. Auto-detected from URL extension if not specified. Use 'none' for direct binary downloads

strip_prefix.description: Directory prefix to strip during extraction. Useful when archive contains a single top-level directory

extract_path.description: Specific path within archive to extract. Defaults to extracting entire archive

permissions.description: File permissions in octal format (defaults to 0755)

custom_commands.description: Custom commands that override default binary installation behavior

download.description: Custom command to download binary. Overrides default wget/curl behavior

extract.description: Custom command to extract downloaded archive. Overrides default unzip/tar behavior

install.description: Custom install command. Overrides default file copy and permission setting

uninstall.description: Custom uninstall command for removing installed binary

version.description: Command to get installed version for tracking

script.description: Script installation configuration for executing installation scripts with security measures

name.description: Logical name for the script installation (e.g., main, official, dev). Used for referencing in template functions

url.description: Script download URL. Should use HTTPS for security. Supports templating with {{version}} placeholder

version.description: Version identifier used in URL templating and for tracking

interpreter.description: Script interpreter. Auto-detected from shebang if not specified. Common values: bash, sh, python, python3

checksum.description: Expected checksum of script file for security verification. Format: algorithm:hash

arguments.description: Arguments passed to the script during execution

environment.description: Environment variables set during script execution

working_dir.description: Working directory for script execution. Defaults to temporary directory

timeout.description: Execution timeout in seconds. Defaults to 300 (5 minutes)

custom_commands.description: Custom commands that override default script execution behavior

download.description: Custom command to download script. Overrides default wget/curl behavior

install.description: Custom install command that completely overrides script execution

uninstall.description: Custom uninstall command for removing software installed by script

version.description: Command to get installed version for tracking

package_source.description: Package source definition that groups packages from a specific repository with priority and recommendation information. Used when software is available from multiple sources with different characteristics

name.description: Source identifier describing the origin or purpose of this package source

priority.description: Priority order for source selection (1 = highest priority). Higher priority sources are preferred when multiple sources are available

recommended.description: Whether this source is recommended for general use. True indicates the preferred source for most users

repository.description: Repository name to use for this source. References a repository defined in the repositories array

packages.description: List of packages available from this source. Can override package names, versions, or options specific to this source

notes.description: Additional information about this source. Use for version differences, stability notes, or special requirements
examples: Latest upstream version with newest features
Older but more stable version from OS repository
Requires additional configuration for SSL support

repository.description: Repository definition for adding third-party or official software repositories. Includes repository configuration and resource overrides specific to packages from this repository

name.description: Unique identifier for the repository. Used for referencing in package definitions

url.description: Repository URL. Format varies by package manager (apt: deb URL, dnf: baseurl, brew: tap URL)

key.description: GPG key URL or fingerprint for repository verification. Required for secure package installation

type.description: Repository type classification. upstream: official software repository, os-default: OS distribution repository, os-backports: OS backports repository, third-party: community or unofficial repository

components.description: Repository components (Debian/Ubuntu specific). Common values: main, contrib, non-free, stable, testing

maintainer.description: Organization or individual maintaining this repository

priority.description: Priority order for repository selection (1 = highest priority). Used when multiple repositories provide the same package

recommended.description: Whether this repository is recommended for general use. False indicates experimental or less stable repositories

notes.description: Additional information about this repository. Use for warnings, requirements, or special instructions
examples: Official upstream repository - recommended for latest versions
Contains older but more stable versions

sources.description: Source build overrides/additions for this repository

binaries.description: Binary download overrides/additions for this repository

scripts.description: Script installation overrides/additions for this repository

compatibility_entry.description: Single entry in the compatibility matrix defining support for a specific provider/platform/architecture/OS version combination

provider.description: Provider name this compatibility entry applies to

platform.description: Platform(s) this provider supports. Can be a single string or array of strings. Common values: linux, darwin, windows

architecture.description: Architecture(s) this provider supports. Can be a single string or array of strings. Common values: amd64, arm64, 386, armv7

os_version.description: OS version(s) this provider supports. Can be a single string or array of strings. Format: os-version (e.g., ubuntu-22.04, debian-11, macos-13)

supported.description: Whether this combination is officially supported. False indicates known incompatibility

notes.description: Additional information about this compatibility entry. Use for caveats, workarounds, or special requirements

tested.description: Whether this combination has been tested. True indicates verified functionality

recommended.description: Whether this is the recommended provider for this platform/architecture/OS combination

versions.description: Version information for the software. Tracks latest, minimum supported, and LTS versions

minimum.description: Minimum version supported by this saidata configuration

latest_minimum.description: Latest version of the minimum supported major version

security_metadata.description: Security-related metadata for vulnerability management, verification, and disclosure

cve_exceptions.description: List of CVE IDs that are known but accepted/mitigated. Used to suppress false positives in security scanning

security_contact.description: Email address or URL for reporting security vulnerabilities

vulnerability_disclosure.description: URL to the vulnerability disclosure policy or security advisories page

sbom_url.description: URL to the Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) document. Can be in SPDX, CycloneDX, or other formats

signing_key.description: GPG/PGP public key fingerprint or URL for verifying package signatures

urls.description: Collection of relevant URLs for the software. Provides links to documentation, source code, support, and other resources

source.description: Source code repository URL (GitHub, GitLab, etc.)

issues.description: Issue tracker URL for bug reports and feature requests

sbom.description: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) URL. Deprecated - use security.sbom_url instead

icon.description: Icon or logo image URL for UI display
